source: no published source; read from the installed 2.1.3 plugin.dylib, which carries full local symbols

lines: A one-voice sample player holding twenty-five LinnDrum drum sounds in five banks, fired from a jack or from the button on the panel
Note — The screen across the top shows the name of the chosen bank and the name of the chosen sample. It is a display rather than a control and cannot be clicked.
Note — The decay knob comes up fully anticlockwise, which cuts every sample off about a seventh of the way through. Turn it almost all the way up to hear a whole sample.
Chooses one of the five banks: Kick&Clap, Snare, Toms, Hat&crash and Extras
Plays the chosen sample once each time it is pressed
Chooses one of the five samples inside the bank
Sets the playback speed, 1 being the speed the sample was recorded at and 2 playing it eight times faster; the scale follows the cube of the setting
Sets how much louder the sample plays when the accent input is high as the trigger arrives, up to 70% above the ordinary level
Turned past halfway, the sample is read a whole step at a time with no interpolation, which roughens it at speeds away from normal; below halfway it changes nothing
Shortens the sample with a straight fade to silence; fully anticlockwise it cuts the sound about a seventh of the way through, and almost fully clockwise the whole sample plays
Read at the moment the trigger arrives: above 0.5V the sample plays at the louder level set by the Accent knob
Plays the chosen sample once when it rises past 0.5V
Adds to the playback speed set by Tune, a fifth of the recorded speed per volt, with the total held at a twentieth of the recorded speed or above
Stops the sample dead while it is above 0.5V
Read at the moment the trigger arrives: above 0.5V the sample plays backwards
Makes the fade quicker, a tenth of the decay knob's travel per volt
Steps on through all twenty-five samples from wherever the bank and sample knobs have left the choice, 2.5 samples per volt
The chosen sample, five times the level it is stored at and half as much again, so a full-scale sample peaks near 7.5V and more with accent

1.why: LDrum::process +0x4998 reads inputs[1].voltages[0] and +0x49a0 tests it against 0.5, combined at +0x49b0 with the same test on the panel button

2.why: LDrum::process +0x4a54 reads inputs[2].voltages[0], multiplies it by 0.2 at +0x4a64 and adds it to the cube of the Tune knob, with the sum floored at 0.05

3.why: LDrum::process +0x4868 reads inputs[3].voltages[0] and +0x4a3c tests it against 0.5, passing the result to DualSampler::process, which stops playback at +0x4f80

4.why: LDrum::process +0x486c reads inputs[4].voltages[0] and +0x49f8 tests it against 0.5, storing the result only on the frame a trigger starts

5.why: LDrum::process +0x4820 reads inputs[5].voltages[0], multiplies it by 0.1 at +0x4830 and adds it to one plus a tenth less the decay knob, with the total floored at 0

6.why: LDrum::process +0x484c reads inputs[6].voltages[0], multiplies it by 2.5 and truncates it, then adds it to five times the bank plus the sample with the total clamped to 0 and 24

Hora-PCMDrumLDrum.notes: HORA PUBLISH NO SOURCE, BUT THIS BINARY IS NOT UNREADABLE. nm on the installed 2.1.3 plugin.dylib returns 527 symbols, and LDrum::process, LDrum::LDrum, DualSampler::process, DualSampler::LoadSamples and screen_LDrum::draw are all present and readable. Everything here was read from that code; the maker's manual page was not used, and check_numbers was not needed. The five bank names are inline immediates in the constructor at +0xcef8 to +0xcf70, written into a table at module+0x970 with a stride of 0x18: Kick&Clap, Snare, Toms, Hat&crash and Extras. The sample number is five times the bank plus the sample knob plus the truncated sample CV, clamped to 0 and 24 at +0x4920. THE DECAY KNOB RUNS BACKWARDS FROM WHAT ITS NAME SUGGESTS AND ITS DEFAULT IS THE SHORTEST SETTING. LDrum::process +0x4800 computes 1.1 minus the knob, plus a tenth of the decay CV. DualSampler::process +0x50c8 leaves the sample untouched when that figure is 0.12 or less, and otherwise applies a straight fade of one minus six times the figure times the fraction of the sample played. With the knob at its default of 0 the figure is 1.1, so the fade reaches silence at about 0.15 of the sample; the fade is skipped only above about 0.98 of the knob's travel. The LoFi knob is configured as a continuous 0 to 1 parameter but is only ever compared against 0.5 at +0x4a44, so it behaves as a two-position switch: above halfway DualSampler reads the nearest stored sample, below halfway it interpolates between neighbours. Playback speed is the cube of the Tune knob, which is configured 0 to 2 with a default of 1, plus a fifth of the pitch CV, floored at 0.05; the samples are stored at 44100 and the step is scaled by 44100 over the engine rate at +0x4f3c. The accent and reverse inputs are levels read once, on the frame the trigger starts, not edges of their own. One light is configured, held at 5 while a trigger is high. There is no context menu. Panel lettering came from res/lowFiDrum.svg rendered with rsvg-convert: BANK, SAMPLE, Tune, Accent, LoFi, Trig, Choke, Rev and Out, with the decay knob marked only by a curve and the trigger button unlabelled. The maker's tooltips use different words again: FREQ for the knob the panel prints Tune, ACC for Accent, DECAY for the unmarked knob, and the input names carry the misspelling 'trigerring'.
